prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in _handle_reconnection ultimately fails (retries exhausted or an error is raised during a reconnect attempt), the caller's pending request is left hanging forever because the failure was never communicated back through the read stream. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in _handle_reconnection ultimately fails (retries exhausted or an error is raised during a reconnect attempt), the caller's pending request is left hanging forever because the failure was never communicated back through the read stream. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same failure path in _handle_reconnection but resolve it differently. #2395 builds a JSONRPCError keyed to the original request's id and sends it via ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the specific in-flight request that depended on the dropped SSE stream gets an error while the rest of the session keeps running; the change is ~12 lines confined to _handle_reconnection and guards against sending an error response for non-request messages. #3098 instead adds a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to pull a StreamableHTTPError out of an anyio ExceptionGroup and raise it; because _handle_reconnection executes inside a TaskGroup-spawned task, raising there propagates as a task-group cancellation, which would tear down the entire client session rather than fail just the one affected request. #3098 also bundles an unrelated change (dropping the `as _annotations` alias on the `__future__` import) into the same diff, mixing an unrelated cleanup with the bug fix.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in pre_parse_json: it JSON-decodes string parameter values whenever the annotation isn't exactly `str`, so a union type like `str | None` causes legitimate strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "[1]") to be silently corrupted into int/None/list before Pydantic validation ever sees the original string. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in pre_parse_json: it JSON-decodes string parameter values whenever the annotation isn't exactly `str`, so a union type like `str | None` causes legitimate strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "[1]") to be silently corrupted into int/None/list before Pydantic validation ever sees the original string. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` calls get_origin(annotation) directly without stripping Annotated first, so for the idiomatic `Annotated[str | None, Field(description=...)]` pattern (used throughout mcpserver tool signatures for documented params), get_origin returns the Annotated special form rather than the union, is_union_origin() is False, and the function falls through to `return True` -- meaning the fix does not actually trigger for the most common real-world case that motivated this bug. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip Annotated before checking for `str | None`, so it correctly fixes the case #2032 misses. #2032 does have broader scope (skips pre-parsing for any union of only simple scalar types, e.g. str | int | bool, not just str | None), so that generalization would be worth re-adding as a follow-up on top of #3056's Annotated-aware base, but as submitted #2032 leaves the common annotated-parameter case unfixed.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in pre_parse_json: it JSON-decodes string parameter values whenever the annotation isn't exactly `str`, so a union type like `str | None` causes legitimate strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "[1]") to be silently corrupted into int/None/list before Pydantic validation ever sees the original string. (2 PRs)
members.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in pre_parse_json: it JSON-decodes string parameter values whenever the annotation isn't exactly `str`, so a union type like `str | None` causes legitimate strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "[1]") to be silently corrupted into int/None/list before Pydantic validation ever sees the original string. (2 PRs)
members.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` calls get_origin(annotation) directly without stripping Annotated first, so for the idiomatic `Annotated[str | None, Field(description=...)]` pattern (used throughout mcpserver tool signatures for documented params), get_origin returns the Annotated special form rather than the union, is_union_origin() is False, and the function falls through to `return True` -- meaning the fix does not actually trigger for the most common real-world case that motivated this bug. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip Annotated before checking for `str | None`, so it correctly fixes the case #2032 misses. #2032 does have broader scope (skips pre-parsing for any union of only simple scalar types, e.g. str | int | bool, not just str | None), so that generalization would be worth re-adding as a follow-up on top of #3056's Annotated-aware base, but as submitted #2032 leaves the common annotated-parameter case unfixed.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same failure path in _handle_reconnection but resolve it differently. #2395 builds a JSONRPCError keyed to the original request's id and sends it via ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the specific in-flight request that depended on the dropped SSE stream gets an error while the rest of the session keeps running; the change is ~12 lines confined to _handle_reconnection and guards against sending an error response for non-request messages. #3098 instead adds a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to pull a StreamableHTTPError out of an anyio ExceptionGroup and raise it; because _handle_reconnection executes inside a TaskGroup-spawned task, raising there propagates as a task-group cancellation, which would tear down the entire client session rather than fail just the one affected request. #3098 also bundles an unrelated change (dropping the `as _annotations` alias on the `__future__` import) into the same diff, mixing an unrelated cleanup with the bug fix.

clusters.pick_reason: #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` calls get_origin(annotation) directly without stripping Annotated first, so for the idiomatic `Annotated[str | None, Field(description=...)]` pattern (used throughout mcpserver tool signatures for documented params), get_origin returns the Annotated special form rather than the union, is_union_origin() is False, and the function falls through to `return True` -- meaning the fix does not actually trigger for the most common real-world case that motivated this bug. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip Annotated before checking for `str | None`, so it correctly fixes the case #2032 misses. #2032 does have broader scope (skips pre-parsing for any union of only simple scalar types, e.g. str | int | bool, not just str | None), so that generalization would be worth re-adding as a follow-up on top of #3056's Annotated-aware base, but as submitted #2032 leaves the common annotated-parameter case unfixed.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the same failure path in _handle_reconnection but resolve it differently. #2395 builds a JSONRPCError keyed to the original request's id and sends it via ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the specific in-flight request that depended on the dropped SSE stream gets an error while the rest of the session keeps running; the change is ~12 lines confined to _handle_reconnection and guards against sending an error response for non-request messages. #3098 instead adds a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to pull a StreamableHTTPError out of an anyio ExceptionGroup and raise it; because _handle_reconnection executes inside a TaskGroup-spawned task, raising there propagates as a task-group cancellation, which would tear down the entire client session rather than fail just the one affected request. #3098 also bundles an unrelated change (dropping the `as _annotations` alias on the `__future__` import) into the same diff, mixing an unrelated cleanup with the bug fix.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2962: Both modify the same branch in validate_tool_use_result_messages() in src/mcp/server/validation.py that decides what happens when a tool_use block has no matching tool_result in the next message — but they resolve it in opposite, mutually exclusive ways. #2962 skips the id-matching check entirely when there are no tool_results (gating it with `has_tool_results and`), so no error is raised at all. #3053 keeps the check active but adds an explicit raise when tool_results are missing, producing a clearer error message instead of suppressing it. Applying both is impossible: one branch must either raise or not raise for the identical input case.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041's diff goes further than #3012: beyond the quote-aware comma splitter (_split_www_authenticate_segments, functionally equivalent to #3012's _iter_www_auth_params), it adds _extract_bearer_auth_params which explicitly matches the scheme via partition(" ") and scheme.lower() == "bearer", fixing the substring-match bug (e.g. a scheme token like "NotBearer" being mistaken for "Bearer") that #3012's visible diff does not address. #3041 also appears to handle multiple challenges within a single header by iterating segments to find the first Bearer challenge, a case not shown as handled in #3012's diff.
